'''GNK power droids''', also known as '''gonk droids''', were an [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] knockoff of the successful [[EG-6 power droid/Legends|EG-6]] [[Power droid/Legends|power droid]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Gonk1.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A GNK power droid in Mos Espa]]
GNK power droids were effectively power generators with legs and simple [[Artificial intelligence/Legends|artificial intelligence]] so they could understand rudimentary commands. They were most commonly found on under-developed worlds that did not have an expansive power grid, or in mobile military operations.

They often made a low honking noise that sounded like the word "gonk," resulting in the nickname '''gonk droids''' or simply '''gonks'''. This form of [[Binary/Legends|droidspeak]] was referred to as "[[Gonkian/Legends|Gonkian]]."

==History==
GNK droids have existed at least since the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], during which they were used on many Republic and Imperial worlds.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> Around that time, several GNK droids were modified for holographic advertisement and used to promote a [[Double Sunburns]] performance on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="TORLotS">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Legacy of the Sith]]''</ref>

A [[Standard year|year]] [[23 BBY/Legends|before]] the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Groodo]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]], in his bid to destroy the [[Fondor Shipyards/Legends|Fondor Shipyards]] and [[Fondor Spaceport|Spaceport]], employed, as part of his [[Droid Control Army]], GNK power droids that were modified with [[Repeating blaster/Legends|rapid-repeating blasters]] in their upper casings. [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], joining the [[Mission to Fondor (Separatist Crisis)|mission to Fondor]], handily defeated a GNK attack with [[Mace Windu's lightsaber/Legends|his]] [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], neatly severing the blaster that had emerged from beneath a lid in the droid's upper frame.<ref name="Star Wars Adventures 3: The Hostage Princess">''[[Star Wars Adventures 3: The Hostage Princess]]''</ref>

[[File:RenownGNK-PoNR.png|thumb|right|200px|A GNK power droid.]]
A [[Unidentified GNK power droid/Legends|GNK power droid]] was part of the crew on board the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Renown/Legends|Renown]]'' when it was [[Capture of the Renown|hijacked]] by [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]] forces. While this [[Power droid/Legends|power droid]] survived the hijacking with a number of other [[Droid/Legends|droids]], all living personnel on board were killed or captured. When [[D-Squad/Legends|D-Squad]] arrived on the ''Renown'', they ran into [[BNI-393/Legends|BNI-393]] who brought them back to their [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] where the surviving droids, including this GNK, were hiding. The group later followed a [[Pistoeka sabotage droid/Legends|buzz droid]] through the [[Starship/Legends|ship]]. This droid toppled, whilst the buzz droids attempted to dismantle the unit but failed to do so. After the buzz droids were defeated, they returned to the shuttle and escaped before the ''Renown'' [[Carida Incident|exploded]].<ref name="Point of No Return" />

Sometime after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], rumors began to spread regarding a "[[Cult of the Power Droids]]." Apparently, a pair of GNK power droids would come to one's door and request funding for a fringe religious group. Advice from renowned linguist [[Ebenn Q3 Baobab/Legends|Ebenn Q3 Baobab]] was that one should merely utter the phrase "Gonk. Gonk. Gonk ko kyenga see," a highly controversial statement that was not allowed to be legally translated (see [[Baobab Security Directive 51-C]]).

==Behind the scenes==
The GNK power droid derives its name from the "gonk" sound it makes in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|Episode IV]]. The droid was originally called simply a "[[Power droid/Legends|power droid]]," but a newsgroup posting in 1993<ref name="Lugnet">{{WebCite|url=https://news.lugnet.com/general/?n=34495|text=OMG - GONK PROOF (was Re:Google archives Usenet back to '81)|archivedate=20190503175132}}</ref> led to the now-official name becoming quickly popular.

In the [[Star Wars Battlefront (series)|''Battlefront'' series]], gonk droids are called '''Ammunition Droids''' and dispense ammo to the troops who stand near them.

In the ''[[LEGO Star Wars]]'' games, gonk droids are slow-moving, weak, and unable to jump, attack and interact with their surroundings. They can be interacted with, such as being Force Pushed, shot or destroyed. They explode when shot. However, they are invincible when they appear in the [[Dex's Diner/Legends|Dex's Diner]] hub area. Gonk droids are included mainly for the player's amusement, as they are universally ignored by enemies. Gonk droids are also a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] character in [[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'']] version. A "Super Gonk" upgrade can be purchased with in-game currency, permitting the player's gonk droid to run and jump, though not attack. Several gonk droids can be found wandering around the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]].
